$comment: Single source of truth for per-feature stability. Schema and consumers: docs/feature-status.md. statusDefinitions are the canonical user-facing explanations (pill tooltips in the app and on the website). All notes are reviewed by David; keep them honest, one line, and free of "I"/"we" (website voice).

statusDefinitions.alpha: Fresh feature. Should work. Might be broken.
statusDefinitions.beta: Works, but expect rough edges and smaller bugs.
statusDefinitions.stable: Well-tested, mature in the context of the whole app.
statusDefinitions.planned: Not built yet. See the roadmap for timing.

features.name: Search
features.note: Filters, regex, and recent searches over any folder: an indexed one answers in well under a second, an unindexed one gets walked live with results arriving as they are found; one search covers one drive, and the AI query translation still misreads some prompts.

features.name: Select files dialog
features.note: Wildcard and regex matching work well; AI selection is cloud-only and can misread an unusual request.

features.name: Image search
features.note: Search the things (dogs, sunset, document, etc., and also text via OCR) inside your photos and screenshots. You pick which folders to index. Runs on your Mac, fully local.

features.name: Archives
features.note: Browse, create, edit, and extract zip, tar, and 7z archives like folders, including password-protected ones. Also .app and .xlsx, .docx, and .pptx files.

features.name: Operation log
features.note: A durable history of every copy, move, delete, and rename. Pick an operation to see every item it touched, check the ones to roll back, and roll back all of it or only some. Operations that can't be reversed say why. Can be turned off in Settings.

features.name: Multi-rename tool
features.note: Rename a whole selection at once, Total Commander style: name and extension masks, search and replace, case changes, counters, and photo and music details like capture dates and track numbers, with a live preview of every row before anything changes. One Undo reverses the whole batch.

features.name: Ask Cmdr
features.note: Chat with an AI agent about your files. It can find them, look inside them (text, PDFs, photos, archives, etc., even on phones and servers), sees your past operations, knows your important folders, can connect a NAS you saved, and can proactively suggest move/rename/delete/unzip actions, which you can review and approve/reject. Fully optional (you can use Cmdr as just a regular file manager!). It can browse and tag on its own, but anything that changes, opens, or deletes files waits for your yes, and it can't read keys, passwords, or browser data. Can use an on-device model for complete privacy, and nothing reaches a cloud AI until you allow it.

features.name: Network drives (SMB)
features.note: Browsing and fast direct transfers work on common NAS setups, with server-side copies within a share, saved servers and shares, account switching, accented names, encryption (which you can require), DFS namespace roots and links, browsing during a copy, and unreliable servers.

features.name: Android devices (MTP)
features.note: Fast transfers on most devices, but macOS sometimes claims the device first and some phones need a reconnect.

features.name: Android devices (ADB)
features.note: Browse and index a phone's whole filesystem over USB debugging, with the phone's Allow prompt handled right in the pane. Tested on a Pixel; needs Android's platform tools installed.

features.name: SFTP servers
features.note: Save an SFTP server once and open it from the volume switcher, with a root and start folder, free space, SSH host-key checks, key files, and passwords in your Keychain.

features.name: WebDAV servers
features.note: Open Nextcloud, ownCloud, Synology, and other WebDAV servers like folders, with a root and start folder, passwords in your Keychain, and a NAS's self-signed certificate trusted on first use.

features.name: NFS shares
features.note: Open a NAS's NFS exports directly, with no sudo or system mount: browse, copy both ways, rename, and delete, with folders refreshing when another computer changes them. Tested on a Linux NFS server.

features.name: S3 storage
features.note: Browse, copy, move, rename, and delete in buckets on AWS, R2, B2, Wasabi, Hetzner, Google Cloud Storage, Spaces, or any S3-compatible server, with cost estimates at list prices and share links. Tested live on all seven providers.

features.name: Restic backups
features.note: Open a restic backup on any drive or server and browse its snapshots like folders, read-only, then copy files out to restore them. The password stays in your Keychain. Tested on a real NAS repo.

features.name: Git browser
features.note: Browse history, branches, tags, stashes, and worktrees like folders, open any file from them in the viewer, and copy one out. Lists up to 100,000 commits in about a second.

features.name: Local AI
features.note: The on-device model runs fully private on Apple Silicon; being a small model, it sometimes gives odd suggestions.

features.name: Download notifications
features.note: Catches downloads and jumps to the latest with one key.

features.name: Go to folder
features.note: Paste or type any path and jump there, with your recent paths to pick from.

features.name: Dual-pane file explorer
features.note: Two panes, virtual scrolling through 100k+ files, live file watching, and Quick Look. The heart of the app.

features.name: File operations
features.note: Copy, move, delete, rename, and new folders with a live file tree of progress, conflict handling, rollback, a background queue that works with mouse+keyboard, and parallel processing when possible. A drive pulled mid-transfer keeps every original, a NAS that drops off gets waited for (copies, moves, deletes, and zip edits alike), and copies keep dates, tags, and permissions wherever the destination can store them. The most-tested code in the app.

features.name: File viewer
features.note: Opens even 10+ GB files instantly in Text, Binary, Hex, and Media modes, shows Markdown formatted with working links, and has search, word wrap, and support for single lines of any length. Images and PDFs render on servers and phones too.

features.name: Tabs
features.note: Per-pane tabs with pinning, history, reopen closed tab, and moving a tab left, right, or to the other pane by drag or keyboard.

features.name: Command palette
features.note: Fuzzy-find every action with ⌘⇧P.

features.name: Keyboard shortcuts
features.note: Customize any shortcut, with conflict detection and scope awareness.

features.name: Full-disk index
features.note: Covers your drive folder by folder, starting with the folders you use most, then stays current through file system events. A drive unplugged mid-scan marks its index for a fresh pass instead of quietly going short, and indexing pauses while your disk is nearly full. Powers search and folder sizes.

features.name: Drag and drop
features.note: Drag files in, out, and between panes, including to and from Finder and other apps.

features.name: AI rename
features.note: Describe the names you want and Cmdr proposes them, reading the text inside your images. Every row shows the file and the evidence behind its name, you allow, edit, or deny each one, and the whole batch is one click from undone.

features.name: AI file organization
features.note: Say "clean up my Downloads folder" and approve or reject each suggested move.

features.name: More file systems
features.note: SCP, Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, and more.

features.name: Tell me about this
features.note: A card for any file or folder: where it came from, what it really is, what owns it, and what removing it means. With AI on, a short AI take sits beside the facts.

features.name: Plugins
features.note: Extend Cmdr with your own scripts and tools.

features.name: Disk space visualizer
features.note: A built-in treemap to see what's eating your disk.

features.name: Windows and Linux support
features.note: Bring Cmdr to more platforms.
